chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: 'Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Jumahi narrated to me, saying: 'Hisham ibn Salim narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)'

He said: 'When you are afflicted with the people of al-Nasb (those of hostility, especially to the Imams) and their companionship, then be as if you are upon the rib of a camel (enduring patiently), until you arise. Indeed, Allah detests them and curses them. So when you see them conversing vainly in mentioning an Imam from the Imams, then arise, for the Wrath of Allah descends upon them there.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ النَّصْبِ: People of al-Nasb (hostility), specifically those opposed to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الرَّضْفِ: The rib of a camel, used metaphorically for enduring discomfort patiently
key_terms.يَخُوضُونَ: To converse vainly or talk loosely

ai.seo_question: How should a Shia Muslim behave when sitting with people hostile to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the nuanced etiquette of 'al-Jalā' wa al-Judhūr' (mixing with the unrefined) for Shia believers, instructing them to maintain composure like one sitting on a rough stone (al-Radf) to endure the hostility of Ahl al-Nasb. The specific trigger for departure—vain discourse about an Imam—highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the dignity of the Imams' names and status, ensuring that their mention is not trivialized or mocked by the ignorant.
